title: Cap. IX Resp.: with the non-elect God acts from philanthropy, goodness, and admirable mildness — conscience convicts innate contagion or voluntary rebellion
pass_a_gloss: We confess that God deals with the elect alone from highest mercy: but we affirm also that he deals with the non-elect or reprobate not from highest right, but from philanthropy, goodness, and admirable mildness; so that they are convinced in their consciences that they were not driven by God by the decree of reprobation, but by innate contagion or voluntary rebellion, or by both, fell into most deserved death.
pass_b_english: Highest mercy, we grant, is how God deals with the elect alone. Toward the non-elect or reprobate his dealing is not highest right either, but philanthropy (φιλανθρωπία), goodness, and a mildness worth wonder. Their consciences themselves convict them: the reprobation decree did not shove them; innate contagion, voluntary rebellion, or both, brought them into a death they richly deserved.
source_text: Fatemur Deum cum solis electis agere ex summa misericordia: sed affirmamus etiam, agere cum non-electis sive reprobatis non ex summo jure, sed ex φιλανθρωπία, bonitate ac lenitate admirabili; adeo ut convincantur in conscientiis suis se reprobationis decreto non fuisse a Deo impulsos, sed aut innata contagione aut voluntaria rebellione, aut utraque in mortem meritissimam incidisse.
